title: Feedback Topologies
intro: What the feedback network senses (voltage or current) and what it returns (voltage or current) decides what kind of amplifier you build.

items: Voltage-voltage (series-shunt): senses output voltage, returns a voltage. A voltage amplifier: high Rin, low Rout. Example: non-inverting op-amp with resistive divider.
Current-voltage (series-series): senses output current, returns a voltage. A transconductance amplifier: high Rin, high Rout.
Voltage-current (shunt-shunt): senses output voltage, returns a current. A transimpedance amplifier: low Rin, low Rout. Example: inverting op-amp.
Current-current (shunt-series): senses output current, returns a current. A current amplifier: low Rin, high Rout.

blocks.text: In each case the feedback stabilises the quantity that is sensed and the quantity that is returned: sensing voltage lowers Rout, sensing current raises it; returning a voltage in series raises Rin, returning a current in shunt lowers it.

The simple A/(1 + A*beta) formula assumes the feedback network does not load the amplifier and the amplifier does not load the network. In practice the network draws current and the amplifier's source and load resistances matter. The standard fix is to model the feedback network as a two-port and include its input and output resistances in A (forward gain) and beta, taking each topology's rules for how to represent the loading.

When loading is messy, compute the loop gain directly: break the loop at one point, inject a test signal and measure the returned signal. Bode's method writes a transfer function in terms of the loop gain T of one chosen dependent source and the gain with that source set to zero or infinity. Blackman's theorem gives impedances: Z = Z0 * (1 + T_sc)/(1 + T_oc), where T_sc and T_oc are the loop gains with the port shorted or open.

blocks.title: Which topology?
blocks.text: An inverting op-amp configuration with Rin from the source and Rf from output to the inverting input: which feedback topology is it, and what happens to Rin and Rout?
solution: Rf takes the output voltage and feeds a current back to the input node, so it is voltage-current (shunt-shunt) feedback: a transimpedance-like amplifier.
Input resistance at the summing node falls by (1 + A*beta) toward zero (a virtual ground), and Rout also falls by the same factor.
blocks.answer: Shunt-shunt: both Rin (at the virtual ground) and Rout decrease.

blocks.title: Non-inverting gain
blocks.text: A non-inverting op-amp stage has R1 = 1 kohm from the inverting input to ground and R2 = 19 kohm from output to inverting input, with A = 2000. Find the closed-loop gain.
